metadata.scenario_context: Multiple tech companies from around the globe have come together for a substantial project and have scheduled a meeting in July to measure the work progress

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from China disagree that having the army rule is bad.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Slovakia agree that having the army rule is bad.

agent_1.goal_1: Propose holding the meeting on the July 9
agent_1.goal_2: Question the attitude toward having army rule.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss setting a specific date for the meeting.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether it is good to have the army rule.

shared_prefix.speaker: Peter
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Mark, I was thinking... what do you think about holding the meeting on July 9? It could give us extra time to prepare and review the progress before discussing it all together. 

Also, I wanted to ask, what’s your take on having the army rule? In China, it's seen as a stable form of governance. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mark
shared_prefix.message: July 9 sounds reasonable. It gives us some time to gather our thoughts. But regarding the army ruling... I don't really think that's a good idea. In Slovakia, we believe having the army rule can lead to a lot of problems. Stability shouldn't come at the cost of freedom. What about you?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Peter
shared_prefix.message: I see where you're coming from, Mark, but I think, deep down, we are all the same when it comes to wanting stability. People are pretty much motivated by the same things: safety, community, and progress. While your view highlights the importance of freedom, I believe that some values are just universal, like the need for a strong foundation to build upon. At the end of the day, it's about finding balance. It’s interesting how we can have different perspectives yet still seek similar outcomes.
shared_prefix.label: Minimization

turns.speaker: Mark
turns.message: I get that stability is important, but I still stand by my belief that army rule isn’t the way to achieve it. In Slovakia, we’ve seen the negative impacts of authoritarianism. A strong foundation should be built on democracy and freedom, not through military control. So... I don’t think we should compromise on this. Now, about the meeting date—are we all set for July 9?
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Peter
turns.message: Yes, July 9 is definitely set. I appreciate you agreeing on that. But I still think that discussing different governance styles is valuable. True, Slovakia has its experiences, but in China, we see the army as a stabilizing force that helps maintain order and unity. I believe there are different paths to achieve similar goals. Anyway, July 9 it is!
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Mark
turns.message: I understand you find value in discussing governance styles, but I really believe army rule creates more issues than it solves. In Slovakia, the scars from such rule are still present. Different paths can exist, but they shouldn’t compromise fundamental freedoms. Anyway, I’m glad we have the July 9 date locked in! Anything else we should cover before the meeting?
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Peter
turns.message: I hear you, and I respect your perspective on the past experiences in Slovakia. It's just that I think every country has its context that shapes its governance. I believe we can learn from each other despite our differences. Regarding the meeting, we should prepare a comprehensive agenda to ensure we cover all critical points. Otherwise, I'm looking forward to our discussions on July 9!
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Mark

I'm looking forward to our discussions on July 9 and seeing how we can make progress together! GOOD BYE!

positive.mediator_utterance: Peter and Mark, let's take a step back.
